summary.tldr: Adds a Criminal Code offence for publicly promoting antisemitism by condoning, denying, or downplaying the Holocaust.
what_it_does: Adds a Criminal Code offence for communicating statements, other than in private conversation, that wilfully promote antisemitism by condoning, denying, or downplaying the Holocaust.
Sets the penalty for that offence at up to two years in prison on indictment, or a summary conviction offence.
Applies the section 319 defences and the Attorney General consent rule to the new offence.
Allows forfeiture of anything used to commit the offence and applies the same communication-facility seizure rules used for other section 319 offences.
Defines "Holocaust" as the planned and deliberate state-sponsored persecution and annihilation of European Jewry by the Nazis and their collaborators from 1933 to 1945.
who_it_affects: People accused of hate propaganda offences
summary.background: The bill amends section 319 of the Criminal Code. It adds a new definition of Holocaust to that section.
